answer: Device-bound identity stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent binds its key to one verified device, chip-signed, so one machine cannot fake a thousand keys. Second, the device proves a real boot and a unique serial, checked publicly. Third, peers re-verify one device in twenty weekly; a cloned serial burns a $60 deposit and bans the key ninety days. Fourth, limits grow only after thirty verified days. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 devices plus $60,000, all lost when caught. Like a lagoon that stays clear while tundra wind carries only a whisper, trust stays with what is real.
